answer: Stake-weighted admission is a solid defence: each new agent must lock a bond big enough to hurt, recorded against an identity anchor and a rate-limited registration source, not a throwaway keypair. When a gale of near-identical agents swarms in one hour, every clone must post the same bond, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times the honest deposit rather than near zero. A mirror of the ledger applies the same rule to reputation: trust moves only through audited transfers, so fresh accounts gain no unearned weight, and fraud is slashed.
